title: feat(expression): current_user.hasCapability answers from the viewer's systemPermissions (objectui#13006)
body:
Fixes #13006
Clause-②: yes

`current_user.hasCapability('NAME')` now answers in the console's predicate scope, from the `systemPermissions` list of the same `/auth/me/permissions` answer the action gate reads. This is the objectui half of objectstack-ai/objectstack#24414 (engine change `ca426cb65d`, already in objectui's pin `f4755a68a7`).

## What changed

- **`@object-ui/core`**, `evaluator/subjectPermissions.ts`: a second `Symbol.for` subject key, `SUBJECT_CAPABILITIES`, with `bindSubjectCapabilities` / `subjectCapabilitiesOf` beside `bindSubjectPermissions` / `subjectPermissionsOf` (the objectui#4421 carrier). `evaluator/fieldRules.ts`: `evalFieldPredicate` passes `systemPermissions` to the engine beside `permissions`. The engine reads `hasCapability` only from `EvalContext.systemPermissions`, and this is the only place on the predicate path that builds that context. Measured before the change: a list carried in the scope bag or on the subject as a string key reached the engine only as `extra` variables, and the call refused with "carries no capability list".
- **`@object-ui/app-shell`**, `providers/ExpressionProvider.tsx`: `buildExpressionScope` takes `systemPermissions` and binds it onto the one subject, under the symbol. It is not a CEL root and not a readable member of `current_user`; `has(current_user.systemPermissions)` is `false`. The new `useExpressionSystemPermissions` reads `usePermissions().systemPermissions`, so there is no second fetch. It hands the list on only when `useExpressionPermissions` binds the object map from the same answer. Before load it hands on nothing, so the call faults, as `can()` does; it is never defaulted to `[]`. `expressionUser.ts` is unchanged, because the list belongs on the evaluation context and not on `current_user`.
- **Docs**: `content/docs/layout/page-header.mdx` adds one line on `current_user.hasCapability` next to the `can()` section. No Studio hint in `views/metadata-admin` lists `can()`: `git grep` for `current_user.can` outside tests finds only that doc and one error string. So there was no hint to add a line beside.
- Actions' `visible`, the action capability gate (`useCapabilityGate`, `ActionEngine`'s `requiredPermissions`) and the proxy pages are unchanged.
- Changeset: `@object-ui/core` minor and `@object-ui/app-shell` minor.

## Pins

- `packages/app-shell/src/providers/__tests__/hasCapability-13006.render.test.tsx` uses a real `MePermissionsProvider`, `ExpressionProvider` and `SchemaRenderer`, with a page node gated on `current_user.hasCapability('manage_org_users')`:
  - (a) Three principals. The **owner** sees the node. The **plain member** and the **platform admin who is a plain member** do not. None of the three arms reports anything.
  - (b) **Not loaded**: the predicate faults and the diagnostic names it. The node is not silently hidden; the fail-soft node gate shows it, which is the existing node policy. A backend that never reported `systemPermissions` gets the same result.
  - (c) **Controls**: an empty reported list hides the node and reports nothing. `can()` answers as before (edit granted and shown, delete denied and hidden, nothing reported).
  - **Watch item**: a real refetch, driven by an endpoint change, where only the capability list differs. Across every render the list and the map are bound together or not at all. Whenever the list changes, the map changes with it, and the `ActionProvider` runner's `current_user` ends on the new list. A second test covers an answer whose object map the formula adapter refuses: neither half is bound, so the call faults instead of answering from that answer's list.
- `packages/core/src/evaluator/__tests__/subjectCapabilities-13006.test.ts`:
  - bind and strip, and binding composes with the permissions map in either order;
  - not a root or member;
  - held answers true, not held answers false, an empty list answers false;
  - absent faults with "carries no capability list";
  - all four subject aliases answer the same;
  - a list carried under a scope key is not read;
  - `can()` control.

## Ablation (one-off, not committed)

`node scripts/ablation-replace.mjs` from the objectstack checkout deleted the `...(systemPermissions !== undefined ? { systemPermissions } : {}),` line in `fieldRules.ts`. The tool reported the anchor count going from 1 to 0 and the blob changing from `d2a1913c50b9` to `5c640350e4d4`. It then ran both new files, with `@object-ui/core` aliased to `src`, so no build was involved: `Tests 8 failed | 12 passed (20)`.
- Red: the owner, member, platform-admin and empty-list arms of the render test, plus core's held, not-held, empty-list and alias tests.
- Green: the not-loaded arms and the `can()` controls. That is the predicted direction.

The tool restored the file to blob `d2a1913c50b9`, equal to the HEAD blob, and `git diff HEAD` came back empty.

## Gates (all on HEAD `2c0b003d70`)

- Closure build `pnpm --filter '@object-ui/app-shell^...' build`: exit 0.
- `type-check` for `@object-ui/core` and `@object-ui/app-shell`: exit 0. Both run `tsconfig.test.json`, which includes `src/**/*.test.ts(x)`.
- vitest with `--maxWorkers=1`, under the shared lock:
  - the two new files: 20 of 20 passed;
  - `packages/core/`: 207 files and 4034 tests passed;
  - `packages/app-shell/src/providers/`: 32 files and 294 tests passed.
  - **Declared to CI:** the rest of `packages/app-shell/`, because the whole directory does not fit in the foreground cap.
- The pre-tsc battery exited 0: `check:phantom-deps`, `self-import`, `unreferenced-sources`, `doc-example-readers`, `handler-key-reads`, `side-effects-array`, `element-data-source-declaration`, `spec-symbols`, `action-forward-parity`, `designer-field-key-parity`, `icon-record-names`, `i18n-keys`, `i18n-drift`, `i18n-designer-parity`, `control-bytes`, `check-hand-rolled-comment-mask.mjs`, `check-changeset-fixed.mjs`, `check-changeset-presence.mjs`, `check-changeset-no-major.mjs` and `check:new-line-citations`.
- `check:spec-floors` exited 1 with `no-artifact` because it needs a whole-workspace build. Per the dispatch it was recorded and not repaired: NOT MEASURED.
- ESLint, narrowed to the 5 changed source and test files: 0 errors, 19 warnings. The warnings are `no-explicit-any` and `react-refresh/only-export-components`, in the same families as the existing lines of `ExpressionProvider.tsx`. The JSON output counted 5 files. The config enables no type-aware linting (no `parserOptions.project` / `projectService`), so this diff cannot change the verdict on any file it does not touch.

## Acceptance notes

- `console/AppContent.tsx` and `views/RecordFormPage.tsx` build their own object-field evaluators with `createExpressionEvaluator({ ..., permissions })`. They are outside this card's surface, so they do not pass `systemPermissions` yet. An object field's `visibleWhen` naming `hasCapability` therefore faults there, and that gate fails open with a diagnostic. Page nodes, nav entries and actions under `ExpressionProvider` all answer. Wiring those two would be a one-line change at each call site.
